messages.content: Cleveland update: Friday evening airfare jumped again, and Daniel can leave Chicago by 2:30 Friday. Let's make this a driving plan for Dec. 12-14. Can you compare the final hotel choices with total weekend cost? Two adults, one moderate room, Saturday timed tickets at the Cleveland Museum of Art, Sunday lunch downtown, and I want Friday dinner to be easy after a late arrival. Include parking, breakfast, room setup, coffee/fridge if listed, and whether the downtown savings are worth it.

Assuming about $145 for gas/tolls and two nights of local parking, here is the useful comparison:

| Hotel | Est. weekend total | Room / breakfast / basics | Parking + dining | Trade-off |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Glidden House, University Circle | about $655 | Standard queen/king, breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge to confirm | Paid parking around $24/night; restaurants nearby, but verify late Friday hours | Easiest for Saturday museum; 15-min drive to Sunday lunch |
| Courtyard University Circle | about $630 before bought breakfasts, closer to $665 with them | King/queen; coffee and mini-fridge usually listed; breakfast not included | Similar paid parking; on-site Bistro, plus nearby options | Lower sticker rate, but breakfast erases most savings |
| Hampton Cleveland Downtown | about $590 | Queen/king; breakfast included; coffee and mini-fridge listed | Higher downtown parking; better late dinner options; add museum rideshares | Saves around $60-65 after logistics, but less convenient Saturday |
| Drury Plaza Downtown | about $625 | Queen/king; breakfast included; fridge/coffee listed | Downtown valet/self-park; easy restaurants | Nice inclusions, but not much cheaper than University Circle once rideshares are added |

My pick is a refundable Glidden House room if it is near $200 pretax. Use Hampton downtown only if late-night dinner access matters more than staying beside the museum.
So the Hampton downtown savings are really only about $60 after parking and museum rideshares?

Right. The room rate gap looks larger, but downtown parking and the Saturday ride to and from University Circle erase most of it. You gain easier downtown dinner and Sunday lunch logistics, but you give up the simpler Saturday morning and the ability to leave the car parked by the museum area.
How much should I value being in University Circle if we're driving and could just park at the museum?

In December, I would value it fairly highly. It avoids moving the car Saturday morning, another garage, and weather timing around the museum entry. Parking at the museum is doable, but the advantage of University Circle is not cost; it is having Saturday feel settled once you arrive Friday night.
What room should I actually reserve?

First choice: Glidden House refundable standard king or standard queen for two adults, non-smoking, at or under about $200 pretax. I would not pay extra for a suite. Add notes for late Friday arrival, parking instructions, and confirmation of included breakfast, in-room coffee maker, and mini-fridge.
If only a standard queen is available, that is fine. I just don't want two doubles.
Agreed. Book the standard queen if that is the available moderate room. I would skip two doubles unless it is the only refundable option left and the price difference is dramatic.
Courtyard is quoting $178. Is that a better reserve than Glidden at $199?

Not if Glidden includes breakfast. Courtyard saves about $42 on room rate over two nights, but two breakfasts can use that up quickly. Courtyard becomes the backup if Glidden has a strict cancellation deadline, parking is higher than expected, or they cannot confirm the fridge.
Then I’ll hold Glidden and keep Hampton downtown as the backup. Anything else before I put the hold in?

Yes: choose the refundable standard queen or king, confirm the cancellation date, ask for written parking cost and garage directions, and save the breakfast plus mini-fridge/coffee notes. If Friday weather looks bad closer in, the downtown backup does not solve the drive; it only improves late dinner access. For now, Glidden is the room to reserve.

messages.content: Now that Cleveland is basically done, I need to plan Richmond Jan. 21-23 for a site visit. Flying from Chicago to RIC. Thursday morning arts education tour in Jackson Ward, Thursday afternoon East End library partner, Friday debrief near Capitol Square ending before noon. I’d like to avoid a rental car if reasonable, keep hotel near or under $185 before tax, and return Friday after lunch.
I can build that. Are you aiming to fly in Wednesday afternoon or evening, and what time does Thursday’s first stop begin? That will decide whether a late arrival still leaves enough margin.
The tour starts at 9:30 a.m. Thursday. I can leave Chicago after a noon internal call Wednesday. United is fine if comparable, but timing matters more. No checked bag.

Then I would avoid any Thursday-morning arrival. Best flight set:

| Option | Itinerary | Est. fare | Fit |
|---|---|---:|---|
| A | United nonstop ORD-RIC Wed 1:55-4:55; United nonstop RIC-ORD Fri 2:35-3:58 | $326 | Best balance; enough Wednesday dinner time and clean Friday return |
| B | United nonstop ORD-RIC Wed 5:25-8:25; same Fri 2:35 return | $310 | Works, but late arrival makes dinner/check-in less relaxed |
| C | American via CLT Wed 12:35-5:40; Fri 3:20-7:30 | $278 | Cheaper, but connection risk and later Chicago arrival |
| D | Delta via ATL Wed 2:15-7:10; Fri 4:05-7:20 | $304 | Fine backup, longer travel day |

I’d hold Option A if the fare is close to that.
Can you layer in hotels and ground transport? I’m torn between downtown and an airport hotel.

Using Option A at about $326 and a no-car plan:

| Hotel base | 2-night lodging est. | Ground estimate | Trip total est. | Practical notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Hampton Inn & Suites Richmond-Downtown, about $169 pretax | $398 | $100-115 | $824-839 | Breakfast included; coffee and mini-fridge listed; easy Capitol Square; short rides to Jackson Ward/East End; restaurants nearby |
| Homewood Suites Richmond-Downtown, about $183 pretax | $431 | $100-115 | $857-872 | Breakfast included; kitchenette/fridge; more room; top of budget |
| Quirk Hotel Richmond, about $176 pretax | $414 | $105-120 | $845-860 | Better character and on-site dining; breakfast not included; fridge should be confirmed |
| Hyatt Place or Hampton near RIC airport, about $139 pretax | $328 | $140-155 | $794-809 | Breakfast and airport shuttle, but every meeting becomes a longer ride and Friday luggage is awkward |

Downtown Hampton is the practical pick unless the exact East End address is far outside the city.
Hampton downtown looks practical. Is Jackson Ward close enough to walk in January?

It may be walkable depending on the exact address and weather, but for a 9:30 tour I would plan an $8-12 rideshare. That protects the schedule and avoids arriving cold or wet. If the weather is clear, you can decide that morning.
The East End library leg is the bigger concern. No rental still realistic?

Yes, if it is a typical East End branch or partner address. Budget $18-25 each way from downtown and 15-25 minutes. For a 2:30 meeting, request pickup around 1:50. If staff offer a ride from Jackson Ward to the library, take it; otherwise rideshare is still simpler than a two-day rental plus parking.
What would a rental add?

A compact car Wednesday to Friday would likely be $150-190 with taxes, before fuel and any downtown parking. Even with several rideshares, the no-car plan should be $80-130 cheaper and less work. I would rent only if the East End visit moves well outside the city or you add multiple unscheduled stops.
Would the airport hotel make Friday easier for the return?

Not much. Friday’s debrief is near Capitol Square, so an airport hotel means either taking luggage downtown Friday morning or going back to the airport hotel before the flight. From downtown, leave Capitol Square around 12:15 and you should be at RIC around 12:40-12:50 for the 2:35 nonstop.
Good. For the hotel I want breakfast included if possible, plus a coffee maker and mini-fridge in the room.

Hampton fits that best at the quoted price: breakfast included, in-room coffee maker, and mini-fridge listed for standard rooms. Homewood also works and gives you a kitchenette, but it is near the top of the limit. Quirk has better dining style, but it loses the included breakfast and needs a fridge check.
I don’t need character for this one. One queen is fine; king only if same price.

Then book Hampton’s refundable standard queen or standard king, whichever is the same lower rate. Avoid paying for a suite or premium view. Also ask whether they can store a bag Friday after checkout while you are at the Capitol Square debrief.
Will the 2:35 Friday return feel rushed if the debrief ends at noon instead of 11:30?

It is still workable with no checked bag: depart Capitol Square by 12:15-12:20, arrive at RIC around 12:45, and you have roughly 1 hour 45 minutes. It does not allow a long sit-down lunch, but it works for a quick lunch or airport food. If lunch becomes a real agenda item, switch to the later one-stop even though it gets you home later.
I’d rather be back before dinner and keep lunch quick. Which pieces should I hold?

Hold these pieces:

| Piece | Hold |
|---|---|
| Flight | United nonstop ORD-RIC Wed Jan. 21, about 1:55-4:55; United nonstop RIC-ORD Fri Jan. 23, about 2:35-3:58, around $326 |
| Hotel | Hampton Inn & Suites Richmond-Downtown, refundable standard queen or king, around $169 pretax |
| Ground plan | No rental car; rideshare RIC-downtown, downtown-Jackson Ward, downtown-East End, and Capitol Square-RIC |
| Estimated total | About $825-850 before meals, depending on final rideshare pricing |

Before booking, confirm the Hampton cancellation deadline, breakfast inclusion, in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge, bag storage, and the exact East End address.
